core_concepts: Conclusion If we are to think responsibly about the impact of AI on humanity, we must look well beyond today’s technologies
AI’s reach will extend well beyond the automation of current human activity
Profound risks come hand in hand with the great potential benefits of AI
Our job in thinking clearly about AI is ceaselessly challenged by the pace at which technology is advancing
What is perhaps toughest to grasp is that not yet invented technologies, some of which are currently inconceivable, will have far greater impact on us in the 2030s than the tools we have today
To help us cope with all this uncertainty, to stretch our thinking, and to lay some foundations in this quicksand, I call loudly for what-if-AGI?
We are shying away from these difficult questions when we fixate on generative AI, for this is simply the latest AI and certainly not the last
In so doing, we need to understand the context of AI—its history, its trajectory, and the factors that are driving its advance
It would be invaluable also to equip ourselves with a new vocabulary to help us conceptualize and discuss more coherently the seismic shifts that AI will bring to all aspects of our lives
We are still at an early stage in assessing the ramifications of this transformation
Our systems are becoming more capable at an accelerating rate
